scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Global classical solutions of the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system” (preprints/Global-classical-solutions-of-the-three-dimensional-relativistic-Vlasov-Maxwell-system-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 362 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 56691a44941097fa), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every smooth admissible datum (1.2) generates a unique global classical solution of (1.1). For every finite T, this solution satisfies f ∈ C∞ ([0, T] × R3 x × R3 v), E, B ∈ C∞ ([0, T] × R3 x; R3 ), and f has compact phase-space support on [0, T]. The two divergence constraints hold for all time.
